title.narrative: Fostering Green Transition in Petén TEI
Fostering Green Transition in Petén TEI

description.narrative:
Overall Objective
To link socioeconomic development in the Department of Petén with protection of the environment and sustainable use of natural resources with gender and cultural pertinence approach.
Specific Objectives (results) are:
1. Improve policy framework and financing for inclusive green economic development in Petén
2. Increase sustainable production and productivity of agriculture, livestock, forestry and tourism
3. Improve waste and waste water management services in the municipalities of Petén-Itzá basin

Bidraget representerar Sveriges stöd till Team Europe-initiativet i Guatemala – ”Fostering Green Transition in Petén.” Det övergripande målet är att koppla samman Peténs socioekonomiska utveckling med miljöskydd och ett hållbart nyttjande av naturresurser, med ett genusperspektiv och kulturell relevans. Projektet är i linje med tre centrala pelare inom TEI: institutionell förstärkning; utveckling av gröna och inkluderande ekonomier; samt hållbarhet i produktiva och miljömässiga system.

The contribution represents Sweden’s support to the Team Europe Initiative in Guatemala – “Fostering Green Transition in Petén.” The overall objective is to link the socio-economic development of Petén with environmental protection and the sustainable use of natural resources, applying a gender-sensitive and culturally relevant approach. The Project is aligned with three key pillars of the TEI: institutional strengthening; the development of green and inclusive economies; and the sustainability of productive and environmental systems.

sector.narrative: Water sector policy and administrative management

description.narrative:
Results obtained up to date
The Governance Unit of El Bloque (BioItzá, Zotz,Tikal, Yaxhá, Cahuí) was formalized through a memorandum of understanding between CONAP, CECON, PROPETEN, Asociación Bio Itzá, and the Ministry of Culture. This enabled coordinated action in four strategic areas: protected area management, capacity building and research, community outreach, and resource mobilization.
An 80% progress was achieved in automating the licensing process for forest resource utilization under the National Council of Protected Areas (CONAP), marking a significant step toward the automation, simplification, and streamlining of procedures.
Local counterparts were strengthened, including PROPETEN, which received support for the development of its strategic plan, as well as ACOFOP, which was assisted in developing its communication plan and updating its gender strategy.
The productivity and competitiveness of FORESCOM, the industrial and commercial arm of the Peten Forest Concessions, was strengthened, through the donation of a sawmill, which enabled the doubling of its production capacity It is important to highlight that forest management within the forest concessions is a successful model that involves communities, government institutions, and international cooperation. Moreover, all management activities are certified under the standards of the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC).
Twenty one Community Forest Fire Commissions (CIFC) were reactivated, trained and some of them equipped, leading to a decrease in incidents due to the implementation of the Early Warning System for Forest Fires (SATIF), social control mechanisms, and community burning schedules.
The establishment of 16 agroforestry and silvopastoral systems was promoted, covering 90 hectares and benefiting 16 producers, who are now part of an ecological connectivity strategy. 61.79 hectares were linked to the National Forest Institute (INAB) incentive programs.
A cost and profitability analysis tool for agroforestry systems was developed, enabling an initial assessment of their financial viability and potential for banking integration.
In regenerative agriculture, workshops, technical exchanges, and prospecting initiatives were conducted in collaboration with Texas Tech University and Escuela Panamericana El Zamorano.
An Integrated Solid Waste Management Program (GIRS) was successfully developed for the Lake Petén Itzá Commonwealth, which includes the municipalities of San José, San Andrés, Flores, San Francisco, San Benito, and Santa Ana. Complementary actions were undertaken to support the program, including a Green Business assessment aimed at fostering sustainable economic opportunities, infrastructure diagnostics to identify suitable sites for final waste disposal, and waste characterization studies in key municipalities. These efforts generated essential data, enhanced municipal planning capacities, and laid the foundation for sustainable solid waste management strategies tailored to the regions environmental and socioeconomic context, while also facilitating the identification of viable financing options.
The Community Tourism Roundtable of Petén was established, bringing together 23 organizations and institutions, which formulated a 2025 strategic agenda and facilitated the exchange of experiences in regenerative tourism and ecotourism models.
Support for entrepreneurial activities was also provided, with six practical entrepreneurship training workshops focused in financial and entrepreneurial terminology, business plan development, and digital skills enhancement. A total of 43 young individuals participated. Each workshop lasted 17 hours, totaling 51 hours of training across all entrepreneurship modules.
Short term technical training programs in tourism services were implemented. A total of 84 individuals received training, 73% of whom were women. Additionally, 143 individuals received coaching in soft skills such as self esteem, vocational and job orientation, comprehensive sexuality education, and violence prevention.(66% percent of the participants were women)
The introduction of credit card payments via POS terminals at Yaxha-Nakun-Naranjo National Park allowed seven community associations offering tourism services in the area to increase sales related to guiding, aquatic transportation, food, handicrafts, and other services for tourists visiting the region.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
